newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude flat, poor margins deter buyers.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude flat, poor margins deter buyers.

text.p: North Sea crudes were steady but inactive on Thursday with few July cargoes on offer and refineries discouraged by deteriorating margins, traders said.
"Most of the North Sea oil which has to be placed has gone and refiners are pretty well covered for the month," said one.
Aug Brent shed 18 cents to $18.74 a barrel by 1222 GMT on the IPE but cash spreads were holding late Wednesday levels, Aug/Sep talking either side of -3 cents which traded twice in late U.S. dealing.
Brent Contracts for Differences (CFDs) were also little changed, next week's dates (July 07-11) pegged at +5/+10 cents.
With much of the July Brent programme nominated loading dates so far in the hands of one major, and with most of the cargoes thought committed, talk on Dated Brent was thin.
Two July 18-20 cargoes were due to turn wet on Thursday.
Traders said refinery buyers were hanging back despite indications that sellers of late month North Sea cargoes may be prepared to trim their offers.
"There's a bit of Ekofisk around and the sellers may be prepared to come lower but buyers are hanging back because margins got whacked," said a trader.
Hydroskimming margins for a typical Rotterdam refinery turned negative on Wednesday after four straight days of gains in Brent's outright value.
Brent cracking margins were still positive but were over 60 cents below last week's average.
A poorly supplied sour crude market kept differentials firm in the Mediterranean, but the possibility of refinery run cuts was expected to keep a lid on further gains.
Profit margins on Russian Urals slipped further on Wednesday, with cracking margins at 39 cents a barrel and hydroskimming margins at minus 83 cents.
One major Italian refiner was heard to have already cut back runs at its Sicilian plant.
"Margins are very bad," said one trader. "The crude moved up fast and products didn't follow, but next week we could see products following and run cuts should help."
A European major was offering a large July 18-19 Urals at dated Brent -60 cents. Only two or three other large July cargoes were still unsold in July.
Weak margins were also dampening buying interest for West African grades, but most July loaders were already sold, traders said.
"Most of July has been done on a FOB basis," said one.
But a few cargoes already loaded on to ships were looking for homes transatlantic, dealers said.
An Odudu was heard sold on a delivered basis into the U.S. Gulf on Wednesday at WTI minus 50 cents for mid-August arrival. But a Brass River loading July 24-26 was still unsold.
"A couple might struggle unless the East comes back to buy," a trader said.
--Mark Thompson, Rosalind Russell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
